web_title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Mix & Real-World Examples
book_title: Chapter 2: Inside the Snacking Machine — Segments, Geographies & Real-World Economics
question: How does Mondelēz generate its $38.5 billion in revenue across product categories and regions, and what does each segment look like in the real world?

epigraph.quote: Consumers do not buy 'categories' in a 10-K filing; they buy a ₹10 chocolate bar at a Mumbai kiosk or a family pack of Oreos in an Ohio supermarket.
epigraph.author: Consumer Goods Field Manual

web_blocks.html: Mondelēz International sells snack foods in over 150 countries and operates manufacturing and commercial footprints in roughly 80 nations [18, 19]. As of December 31, 2025, the company employed approximately 91,000 people worldwide [18, 19]. Crucially, no single retail customer accounted for more than 10% of consolidated net revenues in FY2025 [18]. That broad customer base insulates Mondelēz from acute customer-concentration risk [18]. Management organizes operations into four geographic reportable segments: Europe, North America, AMEA (Asia, Middle East & Africa), and Latin America [10, 19, 20]. It also tracks commercial performance across five product categories [10, 19, 20]. Together, Biscuits & Baked Snacks and Chocolate generated 80.7% of FY2025 net revenues [10, 19, 20].

web_blocks.html: 1. Biscuits & Baked Snacks ($18,391M, 47.7% of FY2025 revenue) — Concrete Real-World Example: Consider a 14.3-ounce family pack of Oreo cookies or a box of Ritz crackers sold in a U.S. Kroger or Walmart. Picture also a single-serve 7Days croissant bought in a Warsaw convenience store. In the U.S., Oreo's weighted all-commodity volume (ACV) distribution exceeds 95% in food, drug, and mass channels, anchored by center-store shelf blocks [22]. Mondelēz bakes the cocoa wafers and fills the crème at automated regional bakeries across its modernized North American network [12, 22]. Third-party logistics then ship pallets directly to retailer regional distribution centers [12, 22]. Management defends shelf velocity through Price Pack Architecture (PPA), spanning $1.25 convenience sleeves, $4.99 family packs, and zero-sugar variants like Oreo Zero launched in 2026 [12, 22]. Meanwhile, in Europe, the 2022 Chipita acquisition added 7Days ambient croissants and enabled co-branded launches like the Milka Croissant [7, 12]. In Q2 2026, Biscuits & Baked Snacks grew +2.5% organically (+2.1% YTD), with Ritz and Ritz Minis gaining U.S. market share despite soft low-income traffic [12, 23].

web_blocks.html: Seasonality and occasion diversity further distinguish Mondelēz's segment mix from single-occasion food peers. Demand stays fairly balanced across the first three quarters, while Q4 is structurally the largest revenue and cash-flow period [19]. Global holiday gifting—such as Christmas, Diwali, and year-end seasonal assortments—drives that Q4 surge [19]. In addition, the timing of Easter shifts chocolate demand between Q1 and Q2 each year [19]. In FY2025, Q4 alone generated $10,496 million in net revenues (27.2% of full-year sales) and $2,000 million in Free Cash Flow (61.8% of full-year FCF) [10, 13]. By spanning everyday lunchbox biscuits (belVita, Ritz), afternoon energy bars (Clif, Perfect Snacks), tropical impulse chocolate (₹10 Cadbury Dairy Milk), and seasonal gifting (Toblerone, Milka), Mondelēz captures multiple daily occasions across income tiers [19, 22].

2. Chocolate ($12,696M, 32.9% of FY2025 revenue) — Concrete Real-World Example: Walk into a traditional kirana shop in Pune, India, or a Carrefour hypermarket in Paris. In India, Mondelēz sells Cadbury Dairy Milk at ₹10 and ₹20 ($0.12–$0.24) impulse price points [12, 24]. Bars are stored inside company-funded Visi coolers (refrigerated glass-front display units) that prevent tropical melting and lock in prime counter visibility [12, 24]. Cocoa liquor and cocoa butter—sourced via Mondelēz's Cocoa Life network across West Africa, Indonesia, and Latin America—are blended with local milk solids at Indian plants like Sri City [22, 24]. Finished bars then move through 2,000+ distributors to over 5 million retail outlets [22, 24]. In Europe, where Milka and Cadbury lead tablet bars, Mondelēz offset 2024–2025 cocoa inflation with +13.9 pp pricing in FY2025 and Revenue Growth Management (RGM) pack-weight reductions [10, 12]. In Q3 2026, as cocoa eased, it rolled back promotional prices in Europe (-3.7 pp) and launched co-branded Cadbury/Milka Biscoff tablets, lifting volume/mix +1.6 pp [12].

3. Gum & Candy ($4,060M, 10.5% of FY2025 revenue) — Concrete Real-World Example: In October 2023, Mondelēz sold its slower-growing developed-market gum business (U.S., Canada, Europe) to Perfetti Van Melle for $1.4 billion [9]. Management refocused the segment on two higher-return engines: emerging-market gum and mints (Trident in Mexico and Brazil, plus Halls lozenges) and U.S./global chewy candy (Sour Patch Kids and Swedish Fish). In Mexico City, a commuter buys a single 5-piece blister pack of Trident or Halls at a street-corner tiendita or OXXO convenience store [7, 12]. That high-margin, low-cocoa impulse purchase leverages the Ricolino acquisition's 440,000+ point-of-sale route-to-market [7, 12]. In Q2 2026, Gum & Candy was Mondelēz's fastest-growing category at +7.6% organic growth (+4.3% vol/mix) [23]. In Q3 2026, COO Luca Zaramella noted that Trident is achieving record-high market share and penetration across Latin America [12].

4. Meals ($2,384M, 6.2%) & Beverages ($1,006M, 2.6%): These legacy categories act as regional cash generators rather than global growth pillars [19, 25]. Meals consists primarily of Philadelphia cream cheese and Dairylea cheese spreads in Europe and select international markets [19, 25]. By contrast, Kraft Heinz owns the North American Philadelphia business [19, 25]. Beverages houses Tang powdered drinks in Latin America and AMEA, plus Bournvita malted food drinks in India, where a zero-sugar variant launched in 2025 [19, 25].

web_blocks.title: Geographic Profit Divergence: Why North America Margins Matter
paragraphs: Europe is Mondelēz's largest revenue region ($15.03 billion, 39.0%), yet North America ($10.68 billion, 27.7%) is structurally the highest-margin region [10, 21]. North America generated an 17.83% segment operating margin in FY2025 (down from 22.84% in FY2024), versus 12.11% in Europe, 12.42% in AMEA, and 11.61% in Latin America [10, 21].

North America's lower cocoa intensity (heavy biscuit and cracker mix) shields it from cocoa shocks. Still, sluggish U.S. low-income consumer traffic (-2.7 pp vol/mix in FY2025) makes promotional discipline and under-indexed channel expansion vital [10, 12].

web_blocks.html: Customer & Supply-Chain Finance Concentration Check: Although no single retail customer exceeded 10% of consolidated FY2025 net revenues [18], Mondelēz faces concentrated shelf-space and promotional leverage in North American grocery, mass, and club channels where warehouse-delivered biscuits compete for end-cap velocity [12, 22]. On the supplier side, the FY2025 Form 10-K discloses that Mondelēz utilizes accounts receivable factoring and supply-chain finance arrangements alongside $10,139 million in FY2025 accounts payable ($9,510 million as of September 30, 2026) to manage liquidity [10, 29]. Should banking partners or supplier terms tighten, Mondelēz warns it would need to draw on revolving credit or increase borrowings to fund working capital [10].

book_paragraphs: If you want to understand Mondelēz from the inside out, forget the corporate slogans and look at the cash register. In 2025, Mondelēz generated $38.54 billion in net revenues across more than 150 countries, with 91,000 employees and no single retail customer representing more than 10% of sales. That customer diversification is a quiet superpower: unlike many U.S. packaged-food peers that live at the mercy of Walmart's buying desk, Mondelēz's revenue is spread across European grocers, Indian neighborhood kiosks, Latin American convenience chains, and North American supermarkets.

Four out of every five dollars Mondelēz collects come from just two categories: Biscuits & Baked Snacks at $18.39 billion, or 47.7% of revenue, and Chocolate at $12.70 billion, or 32.9%. Gum & Candy contributes $4.06 billion, or 10.5%, while legacy Meals like European Philadelphia cream cheese and Beverages like Tang and Bournvita make up the remaining 8.8%. Let's walk through what those numbers actually look like on the ground.

Start with Biscuits & Baked Snacks. Picture a family shopping in an Ohio Kroger, picking up a $4.99 family-size pack of Oreo cookies or a box of Ritz crackers. Oreo is the world's best-selling cookie, commanding over 95% distribution across U.S. food, drug, and mass retailers. Mondelēz bakes those cookies in automated regional plants, ships them into retail distribution centers, and manages shelf velocity through Price Pack Architecture—varying pack sizes from $1.25 single-serve sleeves to club-store bulk packs. Meanwhile, in Central and Eastern Europe, the 2022 Chipita acquisition put 7Days packaged croissants into thousands of gas stations and corner stores, giving Mondelēz an ambient bakery platform it is now cross-pollinating with Milka chocolate.

Now cross the ocean to a neighborhood kirana shop in Pune, India, to see the Chocolate engine at work. Here, a shopper buys a Cadbury Dairy Milk bar for ₹10 or ₹20—roughly twelve to twenty-four cents. To keep that chocolate from melting in tropical heat, Mondelēz places branded glass-front Visi coolers right next to the shopkeeper's counter. That cooler is physical real estate no local startup can easily displace. In 2025, chocolate revenue jumped 12.9% globally, not because people ate more chocolate, but because Mondelēz pushed through double-digit price increases to cover surging cocoa costs. By the third quarter of 2026, with cocoa easing, management selectively dialed back prices in Europe and watched chocolate volumes turn positive again.

Finally, look at Gum & Candy. Back in 2023, Mondelēz smartly sold off its stagnant developed-market gum business in the U.S. and Europe for $1.4 billion. What it kept were the crown jewels: Sour Patch Kids and Swedish Fish in North America, plus Trident gum and Halls lozenges in emerging markets like Mexico and Brazil. In Mexico, pairing Trident with the 2022 Ricolino acquisition gave Mondelēz massive scale in tiny corner tienditas, helping Gum & Candy post 7.6% organic growth in the second quarter of 2026.

Geographically, Europe is the biggest revenue piece at 39%, followed by North America at 28%, AMEA at 21%, and Latin America at 13%. Emerging markets overall represent nearly 40% of sales and remain the company's primary volume engine. Yet North America is the profit anchor, earning an 18% to 23% segment operating margin compared with 12% in Europe and AMEA. That contrast—high-margin North American biscuits versus fast-growing emerging-market chocolate and impulse candy—defines the operational balancing act we will examine next in distribution and unit economics.

Let's also check how the quarterly numbers in Q3 2026 confirmed that geographic balance. Out of $9.97 billion in third-quarter revenue, Europe contributed $3.55 billion, North America $2.85 billion, AMEA $2.18 billion, and Latin America $1.39 billion. Even though Europe saw reported revenue dip 3.3% because management deliberately dialed back chocolate prices by 3.7 percentage points, European volume and mix actually grew 1.6 percentage points—despite unseasonably hot summer weather that shaved roughly 1% off chocolate demand.

Meanwhile, in Latin America, headline volume looked muted only because Mondelēz is managing hyperinflationary Argentina strictly for cash by pricing aggressively. Strip out Argentina, and non-chocolate volume and mix in Latin America grew 4% to 5% in Q3 2026, led by Mexico, Brazil, and the Andean region. Seeing those regional nuances—India's 130,000 new stores, Europe's volume recovery, and North America's savory cracker strength—shows why a single consolidated growth rate never tells the whole story.

One subtle feature of Mondelēz's revenue engine that often surprises newcomers is its fourth-quarter cash-flow seasonality. On the surface, snacking looks like a smooth, year-round habit. Yet in 2025, the fourth quarter alone delivered $10.5 billion in revenue—27% of the year—and a staggering $2.0 billion in Free Cash Flow, more than 60% of the entire year's cash generation. Why? Because chocolate gifting peaks around Diwali in India, Christmas in Europe and the Americas, and holiday entertaining in the U.S.

That occasion diversity is a quiet moat in its own right. A morning commuter grabs a belVita breakfast biscuit or a 7Days croissant. An afternoon runner reaches for a Clif Bar. A parent packs Ritz crackers or Oreo cookies into a school lunchbox. A traveler picks up a Toblerone bar at an airport duty-free shop. By owning distinct dayparts and price tiers across 150 countries, Mondelēz avoids relying on any single consumer demographic or retail format.

Before we move on to distribution, let's make sure we don't overlook the smaller 8.8% slice of revenue sitting in Meals and Beverages—$2.38 billion in Meals and $1.01 billion in Beverages during 2025. Even though management treats these as regional cash cows rather than global growth engines, they still play an important role in local retail scale. In Europe, Philadelphia cream cheese and Dairylea cheese spreads give Mondelēz refrigerated-aisle presence alongside its ambient biscuit and chocolate racks. In India and Latin America, Tang powdered drink mixes and Bournvita malted beverages anchor family-oriented grocery baskets.

Notice how management is even modernizing those legacy cash cows selectively rather than letting them decay. In India, Mondelēz launched a zero-sugar version of Bournvita in 2025 to address shifting parental nutrition preferences. That kind of quiet SKU maintenance keeps cash flowing out of mature categories to fund growth in biscuits and chocolate.

One subtle nuance behind that no-single-customer-above-10% headline is how Mondelēz finances its working-capital engine. In its FY2025 Form 10-K, management explicitly discloses the use of accounts receivable factoring and supply-chain finance programs alongside $10.14 billion in accounts payable ($9.51 billion at September 30, 2026) to keep cash conversion negative. While that structure is standard for scale consumer staples, it means uninterrupted credit-market and banking-partner terms are essential to preserving working-capital liquidity.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Why Price Pack Architecture Matters More Than List Price
book_callouts.text: When inflation hits snacking, consumers rarely abandon a beloved brand outright; instead, they trade down to smaller packs or wait for promotions. By engineering ₹10 Indian bars, $1.25 U.S. sleeves, and family-pack club formats, Mondelēz protects household penetration during inflationary spikes—which is why volumes snap back quickly once promotional pricing normalizes.
